scope: Session ownership and staged installation of the shared native UI transport host

implementation.separation: Supervisor relays opaque menu addresses; host reuses existing helper and D-Bus binding modules. GNUstep/AppKit controls and native policy remain in the independent UI library.
implementation.capabilities: Two source descriptors are duplicated above child destination slots before installation. Workspace gets independent shell and menu roles; host gets only its private menu role. Capabilities close on subsequent exec.
implementation.readiness: Fresh private directory, mode-0600 listening socket, kernel SO_PEERCRED PID and UID tied to the foreground host. Class user and private D-Bus required.
implementation.recovery: Stable Workspace relay, one in-flight bounded request, serial-correlated replies, latest desired address replay. Three failures disable the optional host. Startup/reply/termination deadlines are bounded.
implementation.availability: Owned GLib context/thread handles availability queries only. Native model, rendering, actions and callbacks stay on the main UI owner thread. X11 registration is explicitly unsupported.
implementation.keyboard: Virtual keyboard insertion/removal updates real seat capabilities; headless test keymap comes from libxkbcommon rather than a copied binding table.
implementation.cleanup: Only the successfully created private runtime is recursively removed, after owned-child teardown, without following symlinks.
implementation.install: ForeignScrollers installs host, reused source modules, shim and independent provider. User launcher selects sibling host when installed; NEXTSPACE_NATIVE_UI=off opts out.
implementation.boundary: Headless staged session with actual Workspace connection classes, not a full installed Workspace/PAM deployment. Existing browser transport reconnection is not implemented.

remaining: Recover surviving browser request, notification and callback sockets after host loss; native menu replay alone does not establish field/global-key recovery.
Automatic browser adapter installation and audited build selection; Chrome, Vivaldi and Firefox derivatives remain unqualified.
Complete browser web/frontend controls, dialogs, IME, accessibility and output scaling.
Full installed Workspace and PAM/login deployment, production backend namespace and complete GTK/Qt Debian package build.
Continue application-wide native integration for GTK, Qt/KDE and other non-GNUstep applications after the browser families.
